name: MN-03
label: Safe D

key_factors: District's strong Democratic lean of about 11 points on the 2024 partisan vote
Incumbent Kelly Morrison running for reelection with a large fundraising edge
Prediction markets price Morrison near 94% to win
Republican challenger Tyler Bass has reported no fundraising
model.rationale: The fundamentals point strongly to Morrison: an 11-point Democratic district, incumbency, and a fundraising advantage of more than $1.3 million raised against a challenger with no reported totals. Markets agree, pricing her around 94%, so the race sits firmly in Safe D territory.
model.watch: Any late surge in outside spending against Morrison or a wave-level shift toward Republicans nationally would be the main thing to watch, though it would need to be unusually large to threaten the seat.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Kelly Morrison, a Democratic incumbent first elected in 2024, is seeking a second term in a Minneapolis-suburban district that voted about 11 points more Democratic than the country in the last presidential election. She has raised roughly $1.4 million and holds about $414,000 on hand, while Republican Tyler Bass has reported no fundraising totals.

No public general-election polls or expert ratings are available for this race, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals, the money gap, and prediction markets, which give Morrison roughly a 94% chance of winning. The seat is rated Safe Democratic, with the main uncertainty being the size of the margin rather than the winner.
